verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 13% to a record $12.1B — even after handing $5.1B back to clients as incentives, about 30 cents of every gross revenue dollar.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees based on payments volume, recognized on the prior quarter's volume — which grew 10%.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for processing transactions on Visa's network — 74.2 billion transactions processed, up 10%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used across borders — cross-border volume rose 14%.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services — risk tools, consulting and newer services — up 40%, the fastest-growing line.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits — Visa's biggest running cost.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — includes a $282M donation of investments to the Visa Foundation this quarter.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Mostly the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case — a legal charge Visa excludes from its non-GAAP results.

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Network and processing ($293M), professional fees ($322M) and depreciation & amortization ($377M).

takeaways.title: A record quarter
takeaways.text: Net revenue hit a record $12.1B, up 13%, on payments volume +9%, cross-border volume +14% and processed transactions +10%. Full-year net revenue grew 15% — the strongest in over 15 years outside the post-pandemic rebound.

takeaways.title: Incentives are the toll
takeaways.text: Client incentives — rebates paid to issuing banks and partners — rose 21% to $5.1B, about 30% of gross revenue. They grow faster than revenue because big clients negotiate harder.

takeaways.title: GAAP understates it
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS of $3.19 includes a $469M litigation provision and a $282M donation to the Visa Foundation. Excluding special items, non-GAAP EPS was $3.48 on net income of $6.6B.

follow100Note: Per $100 of gross revenue (before client incentives). Measured against Visa's reported net revenue of $12.1B instead, the kept profit is $49.44 per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
oneTimers: A litigation provision of $474M (the flagged special item is $469M) for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case — Visa excludes it from its non-GAAP results.

A $282M donation of investments to the Visa Foundation and a $37M deferred tax expense from a change in the U.S. taxation of certain foreign earnings are also excluded from non-GAAP results. Non-GAAP net income was $6,552M ($3.48 per share).
otherDetail: Investment income and other gains of $290M (including $155M of net gains on equity investments), less $192M of interest expense — net +$98M.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $12,139M; this page starts from gross revenue of $17,262M so the $5,123M of client incentives shows as a cost.
